title: Entities and reserved characters
learningObjectives: Choose semantic text elements and inspect their browser output

understand.concept: Character references such as &amp;, &lt; and &gt; represent reserved characters in markup. Prefer literal Unicode for ordinary characters when safe and appropriate.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct escaping prevents text from being mistaken for markup and makes examples readable.
understand.analogy: A book uses headings, paragraphs and notes for different purposes; HTML gives those roles explicit structure.
understand.analogyLimit: The book analogy is a memory aid; a browser parses HTML according to defined rules.

explain.narrative: Character references such as &amp;, &lt; and &gt; represent reserved characters in markup. Prefer literal Unicode for ordinary characters when safe and appropriate.

examples.explanation: Each element gives meaning to its content. Render it in a browser and observe how changing an element affects meaning and presentation.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser displays the corresponding heading, paragraph, inline formatting or text structure.

practise.guidedTask: Inspect the H3.7 concept in the starter code and add one more example.
practise.independentTask: Write a short semantic article on a topic you choose; use CSS rather than misusing HTML for visual spacing.
hints: Choose elements for their meaning, not their default appearance.

practice.starterCode: Use < to display < and & to display &.
practice.resetCode: Use < to display < and & to display &.

questions.prompt: What should primarily guide your choice of an HTML element?
questions.explanation: Semantic HTML communicates the role of content.

questions.prompt: What is appropriate for visual spacing alone?
